facts.statement: Real patient data containing names, DOBs, and diagnosis codes was shared with offshore engineers in Pune, India, before the Business Associate Agreement (BAA) was signed.
facts.quote: Kevin Brooks (their data eng manager) emailed a "sample extract" on 12 Sep so we could size the pipeline. Pranav opened it here and forwarded to Sneha and Vikram in Pune to start profiling. "It's real data I think — names, DOBs, some diagnosis codes."
facts.whyItMatters: Protected Health Information (PHI) was shared and accessed by offshore personnel before a BAA was executed, violating both standard regulatory requirements and the proposed BAA term restricting data access to the US.

facts.statement: A US-based freelance data engineer is being staffed to handle the Harrington work to comply with BAA restrictions against offshore data access.
facts.quote: the BAA says nobody outside the US touches patient data, so he's bringing in Daniel Ortiz, freelance data engineer in Austin. Contractor agreement + NDA drafted on our US template.
facts.whyItMatters: The reviewer must ensure the contractor agreement and a subcontractor BAA are in place for Daniel Ortiz before he accesses any data, especially given the US-only restriction.

facts.statement: Harrington's proposed BAA requires a $5M cyber insurance policy, whereas the current corporate policy is only $1M.
facts.quote: Our cyber policy is $1M btw, Harrington BAA wants 5.
facts.whyItMatters: There is an active liability/insurance gap of $4M that needs to be addressed or negotiated before executing the BAA.

facts.statement: The Harrington MSA and BAA must be finalized and signed by October 1, 2026.
facts.quote: Rebecca needs MSA + BAA by 1 Oct.
facts.whyItMatters: This represents a critical deadline to complete the agreements, resolve the insurance gap, and formalize the contractor's status.
